record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: When a smooth oval is approximated by n-gons and the quality of approximation is measured by the area of the symmetric difference between the oval and the polygon, is the resulting optimal-approximation function of n related to a billiard-type dynamical system?

evidence.quote: Is the resulting function of n related to a billiard-like dynamical system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex compact set (a "smooth oval") with $C^\infty$ boundary $\partial K$. For each integer $n \geq 3$, define
$$\delta(n; K) \;=\; \inf_{P}\, \mathrm{Area}\bigl( (K \setminus P) \cup (P \setminus K) \bigr),$$
where the infimum is taken over all (not necessarily inscribed or circumscribed) convex polygons $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with at most $n$ vertices, and $\mathrm{Area}$ denotes Lebesgue measure of the symmetric difference between $K$ and $P$.

Question: Is the function $n \mapsto \delta(n; K)$, together with the geometry of the optimal approximating $n$-gons (e.g.\ their vertex configurations as $n$ varies), governed by — or naturally identifiable with — the orbits / invariants of some billiard-like dynamical system associated with the oval $K$ (for instance an outer/inner/symplectic billiard map, or a comparable map on $\partial K$ or on chords of $K$)? Equivalently, exhibit such a dynamical system that produces the optimal $n$-gons and the asymptotic behavior of $\delta(n; K)$, or prove that no such billiard-type description exists.
artifact.category_tag: Polygonal approximation of convex bodies and billiards
artifact.status_search_result: Standard asymptotics for best approximation of smooth convex bodies by polygons in the symmetric-difference metric are classical (McClure–Vitale, Gruber: $\delta(n;K) \sim \frac{1}{24 n^2}\bigl(\int_{\partial K} \kappa^{1/3}\,ds\bigr)^3$). However, no source identified in the search establishes (or refutes) a precise correspondence between the optimal $n$-gon sequence and a billiard-type dynamical system on the oval. The question, posed as an open problem on quantitative symplectic geometry / billiards, does not appear to have been resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (R. E. Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of billiard-type dynamical systems associated to convex domains; does not address best polygonal approximation in the symmetric-difference metric.
status_evidence.claim: No identification of optimal symmetric-difference n-gon approximation with a billiard system is reported.

status_evidence.title: On the integrability of Birkhoff billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses inscribed periodic polygonal orbits (extremal perimeter) of Birkhoff billiards in ovals, but not symmetric-difference area minimization.
status_evidence.claim: Known billiard-orbit polygons optimize perimeter, not symmetric-difference area, leaving the stated question unaddressed.
